title: xUnit
description: The default testing framework for .NET Core with a clean, extensible model.

data.text: `xUnit` is the default testing framework for .NET Core. It uses `[Fact]` for simple tests and `[Theory]` for data-driven tests. It is extensible, open source, and built by the .NET team.

data.title: Installation
data.content: Install xUnit and the test SDK.
data.code:
dotnet add package xunit
dotnet add package xunit.runner.visualstudio
dotnet add package Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk

data.text: A test class does not need a special base class. Use `[Fact]` to mark a test method and `Assert` to verify results.

data.title: Basic Fact Test
data.content: A simple xUnit test for a calculator.

data.text: Use `[Theory]` with inline data or a custom data attribute to run the same test with multiple inputs.

data.title: Theory with Inline Data
data.content: Test multiple inputs with a single test method.

terms.definition: An attribute that marks a test method that has no parameters.
An attribute for parameterized tests that run multiple times with different data.
An attribute that supplies inline values for a Theory test.

data.title: Tip
data.text: xUnit runs tests in parallel by default. If tests share state, use `[Collection]` or disable parallelism with `[Collection("Sequential")]`.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: xUnit is the default .NET Core testing framework
Use [Fact] for simple tests and [Theory] for data-driven tests
Tests run in parallel by default
Assert provides a rich set of verification methods
data.takeaway: xUnit is the modern choice for .NET unit testing with excellent parallel support.
